entry.title: What If Your CRUSH Became Your STEPSISTER?

media:group.media:title: What If Your CRUSH Became Your STEPSISTER?
media:group.media:description:
What if your mom fell in love with your crush's dad… and the girl you've liked since seventh grade moved into the room next to yours? Same bathroom. Same family group chat. Same plastic crown on Channel 4.
You've talked to Lila Brandt exactly eleven times. Now she eats cereal standing up in your kitchen, sings badly through a paper wall, and calls you "brother." Her dad sells hot tubs on TV. Your mom hasn't been this happy in four years. Then, at 1:14 in the morning, Lila knocks on your wall with a plan: break up your parents before the wedding.
Operation Cold Water. Salt in the lemon cake. A hundred-question quiz. A freezing hot tub. Your mom's high school ex.
Nothing goes the way it should. And the drawing hidden in your shoebox was never as hidden as you thought.

entry.title: What If Your CRUSH Became Your ROOMMATE?

media:group.media:title: What If Your CRUSH Became Your ROOMMATE?
media:group.media:description:
What if the housing office made one tiny mistake… and your crush became your roommate? Same apartment. Same kitchen. Same bathroom. For a whole year.
You've liked Frankie Reyes for four years. She has never said your name. Now she lives on the other side of a strip of yellow tape, eats hot sauce on her cereal, fixes everything with a screwdriver, and calls you Todd. There are rules on the fridge. Rule number five: don't get weird.
Then you find out the mistake wasn't a mistake.

entry.title: What If You Had 999 Charisma in High School?

media:group.media:title: What If You Had 999 Charisma in High School?
media:group.media:description:
First day of freshman year. Eighteen hundred kids in the gym, a dead microphone, and a principal yelling "Sutton! Fix it!" at the sound table. Then three lines of white text float in front of your eyes, like the choices in a video game. Next to each one: one hundred percent.
You have 999 charisma. Whatever line you pick, it works. On the seniors, on three thousand people at a football game, on a car salesman, on the principal himself. There's only one person you promise never to use it on: Margo Sutton, the sophomore who runs the sound, hates microphones and has never once made the yes face.

entry.title: What If You Got Trapped in an Escape Room With Your Crush?

media:group.media:title: What If You Got Trapped in an Escape Room With Your Crush?
media:group.media:description:
It's Mila Petrova's 13th birthday party, and the main event is Heartlock: a love-themed escape room with a heart-shaped door, a fortune-teller quiz, a dance floor that lights up and a Tunnel of Love with a swan boat. Twelve people are watching on a screen in the lobby. And the person locked in there with you is Ivy Marsh, the girl who has beaten you at everything since kindergarten.
You have 60 minutes. With 72 seconds left, a storm knocks out the power, the door locks, and the longest night of your life begins.
Would you read your crush's answers if they were right there in a mirror?

entry.title: What If You Woke Up 10,000 Years Ago With Your Crush?

media:group.media:title: What If You Woke Up 10,000 Years Ago With Your Crush?
media:group.media:description:
What if you woke up ten thousand years ago, with your crush? You open your eyes at the mouth of a cave, with a spear poking your cheek and a man wearing an entire deer on the other end of it. Next to you: Ellie Novak. Front row in history. White puffer jacket. Phone at a hundred percent.
You have one month, until the moon is full. No Wi-Fi, no chargers, no bathroom. A tribe that has never seen a zipper. A girl called Ika who has decided you're hers. And a cave wall full of red handprints that nobody has ever been able to explain.

entry.title: What If You Got Stuck in a Walmart With Your Crush for 30 Days?

media:group.media:title: What If You Got Stuck in a Walmart With Your Crush for 30 Days?
media:group.media:description:
What if you got stuck in a Walmart with your crush? Not for one night. For thirty days. Every snack, every toy, every shopping cart in the building. And nowhere to hide when it gets awkward.
You're the cart boy. The lowest job in the whole store. Then a flash flood hits the town, the manager takes the last bus out, and the only two people left inside are you and Nina Castillo, the girl who sits two rows in front of you in math. The girl who never puts her cart back.
You build a fort out of water bottles. You race shopping carts down Action Alley. You turn forty mannequins to face the wall, except Kevin. And every night at nine, a voice comes out of the speakers: "Attention shoppers."

entry.title: What If You And Your Crush Were Alone On A Desert Island?

media:group.media:title: What If You And Your Crush Were Alone On A Desert Island?
media:group.media:description:
What if you and your crush were alone on a desert island? No phones. No parents. Just the two of you, one cracked kayak, one emergency flare, and a four-metre crocodile who thinks the island belongs to him.
The wind pushes your kayak out to sea all night, and at six in the morning it cracks on a rock in front of a tiny green island. Sitting in the front is Ruby Cole. Your mums are best friends, she pushed you into a pool when you were six, and she hasn't spoken to you since Year Seven. You've had a crush on her for two years.
Thirty-nine days. Coconuts that go straight through you, one toilet called "behind the big rock", a gang of monkeys that steal your only flare, a storm, a sea urchin, and a boat made from a kayak, two logs and eleven hair ties. And every afternoon at ten past four, a plane that never waves back.

entry.title: What If You Became Stronger Every Time Someone Hurt You?

media:group.media:title: What If You Became Stronger Every Time Someone Hurt You?
media:group.media:description:
What if every punch, every laugh behind your back and every "you can't sit here" made you stronger? Not just the hurts that leave a bruise. All of them. And the ones nobody can see count the most.
You're thirteen, you weigh 38 kilos, and every morning at the school gate Brandon Shaw flicks your ear. Then, one Tuesday, after three dead arms behind the science block, you lock yourself in the boys' toilets and find a muscle that wasn't there this morning. Six years later, sixty thousand people are shouting the name he gave you.

entry.title: What If You Were Trapped in Squid Game With Your Crush?

media:group.media:title: What If You Were Trapped in Squid Game With Your Crush?
media:group.media:description:
What if you got stuck in Squid Game with your crush? Not watching it. In it. Four hundred and fifty-six players, six games, one giant piggy bank. And on the shelf across from yours, number 107: Nora Hale, the girl you've sat behind in chemistry for two years without saying a single word.
Red light, green light. A sugar biscuit and a needle. A carousel where a number decides whose hand you grab. A glass bridge where one panel holds you and one doesn't. And at the end, a vote, with forty-five million pounds in the piggy bank and two players left.

entry.title: What If You Were Stuck in a Bunker With Your Crush?

media:group.media:title: What If You Were Stuck in a Bunker With Your Crush?
media:group.media:description:
What if you got stuck in a bunker with your crush? Not for an hour. For three months. With no signal, one bucket, and nowhere to go when it gets awkward.
A volcano goes off two hundred miles away, the whole school runs, and you're the only one who knows about the old bunker under the park. You've spoken to Ivy Marsh four times. Two of them were "sorry".
Ninety days. A fan you turn by hand, a water filter called Dennis, a toilet behind a shower curtain with ducks on it, and a sign you painted when you were twelve: KEEP OUT. NO GIRLS.

entry.title: What If You Could Talk To Any Animal?

media:group.media:title: What If You Could Talk To Any Animal?
media:group.media:description:
What if you could talk to every animal on Earth? For three years, a seagull called Gary has stolen your breakfast. This morning, he looks at you and says, "Morning."
You're fifteen. You've got four rules, a best friend who's scared of anything with more than two legs, a bully with a moustache he's very proud of, and a leaflet on your bed called "Feelings and You". Before the end of the year, you'll cross the open sea on the back of a whale. At night. In a storm. On purpose.
Flies only ever say one word, and the word is "bin".

entry.title: What If a Caveman Woke Up in Today's World?

media:group.media:title: What If a Caveman Woke Up in Today's World?
media:group.media:description:
What if a caveman suddenly woke up in today's world? Imagine going to sleep 10,000 years ago and waking up in 2026.
No more hunting for survival. No more living in caves. Instead, you're surrounded by smartphones, skyscrapers, cars, airplanes, artificial intelligence, and technology that would seem like pure magic.
How would a prehistoric human react to the modern world? Would they understand our technology? Could they learn to use a smartphone? And how long would it take them to adapt to modern society?
In this video, we explore what would happen if a caveman suddenly appeared in the 21st century — from their first encounter with a smartphone to discovering electricity, the internet, modern food, and the incredible world humans have built.
Would they be amazed by our civilization, or completely terrified?

entry.title: What If You Knew the Exact Date of Your Death?

media:group.media:title: What If You Knew the Exact Date of Your Death?
media:group.media:description:
What if you knew the exact date of your death? Would you live differently, take more risks, or spend every day counting down to your final moment?
Imagine waking up tomorrow and discovering the exact day your life will end. No uncertainty. No surprises. Just a countdown you can never escape.
Would knowing your death date make you appreciate life more, or would it slowly destroy your happiness? Would you quit your job, travel the world, confess your feelings, or try everything possible to change your fate?
In this video, we explore one of the most fascinating thought experiments imaginable: what happens when humans know exactly when they're going to die?
From the psychological impact of knowing your future to the choices you might make with your remaining time, this scenario will make you question everything you thought you knew about life and death.

What if the Sun suddenly went dark tomorrow? No sunlight. No warmth. Just a world slowly falling into darkness.
At first, everything might seem normal. But within hours, temperatures would begin to drop, ecosystems would collapse, and humanity would face one of the most terrifying survival scenarios imaginable.
How long would Earth stay warm? Could humans survive without sunlight? And what would happen to our planet after days, months, or even years of darkness?
